Ravi P: Throwing a different decomposition on the table: prefilter -> normalizer -> ranker -> tie-breaker. each step tiny and testable.
Elaine M: curious why prefilter first? isn't matching same thing?
Ravi P: prefilter = eliminate obviously incompatible routes (quota, region lockdown, capability mismatch). keep it cheap. normalizer = convert heterogeneous signals into a common cost metric (cost/latency/penalty). ranker then sorts by normalized score. tie-breaker applies fairness or tenant-priority.
Corey (policy): love the separation. main win: easier unit tests + safer hot reloads since prefilter changes less often. also lets us persist normalized baselines for quick fast-paths.
Nora - Metrics: question for ops — how do we surface drift between normalized baseline and live signals?
Ravi P: we emit `baseline_normalized_score` + `live_adjusted_score` per-decision. drift metric = p99(|baseline - live|). alert if > X% for 5m.
Sam W: implementation detail: prefer immutability for route templates. normalizer references template_version so invalidations are simple.
Elaine M: tie-breaker... we need reproducible ordering for debugging. propose deterministic shuffle seed derived from request_id for fairness bucketing.
Corey (policy): agree. also need to keep outcome explainable: `explain = [{step: 'prefilter', reason}, {step:'normalize', value}, {step:'rank',score}]`. Console wants short human reasons.
Ravi P: API sketch:
```
PolicyPipeline.Evaluate(req) -> {candidates:[{id}], explain:[...], tags:[policy_version, template_v]}
PolicyPipeline.ScoreBatch(reqs, signals) -> [{req_id, ranked:[id], latency_ms}]
```
Nora - Metrics: add `pipeline_latency.{prefilter,normalize,rank,tie}` and `pipeline_cache_hit`
Elaine M: caching strategy? normalized baseline seems cacheable per (tenant, model, template_v). but live signals must be separate.
Ravi P: exactly. cache normalized baselines with TTL and version-based invalidation. overlay live signals at runtime — do not bake them into the cache keys.
Corey (policy): what about strong consistency during template promotion? race between old cached baseline and new template.
Sam W: on promotion we push `template_promotion_marker` and do two-phase invalidation: 1) mark stale 2) async purge. in meantime ranker checks marker and forces re-eval if stale.
Elaine M: correctness vs perf: if ranker forces re-eval often, we'll lose perf. metrics will tell.
Nora - Metrics: add `promotion_inflight_reval` gauge.
deploy-bot: canary scheduled for group alpha at 03:00 UTC tomorrow :rocket:
Corey (policy): rollout plan idea: shadow mode for 48h (write explain logs) -> small canary -> 1% traffic ramp every 6 hours -> full.
Ravi P: fallback semantics: if normalizer fails or times out -> fallback to `static_score` from template + tag explain=`normalizer_timeout`. if ranker times out -> fallback to cached baseline order.
Sam W: perf SLOs: prefilter p50 < 0.5ms, normalize p50 < 1ms, rank p50 < 2ms, overall p95 < 10ms.
Elaine M: tests to add: mutation tests for template updates, determinism tests for tie-breaker, integration with KV invalidation.
Corey (policy): I'll draft RFC with diagrams + sample payloads. want me to include code stub for normalizer?
Ravi P: please. keep stubs in TS + Go. also include a small simulation harness to replay traffic and compute drift stats.
Nora - Metrics: I'll draft dashboards: drift heatmap, per-step latency waterfall, promotion_inflight_reval.
Sam W: cool — tag me for RFC review. I'll run core canary. :thumbsup:
